capture.title: Spike: Android hardware H.264 capture with original sensor evidence
capture.description:
## Outcome

Decide whether the available Android phone can sustain the proposed hardware H.264 plus AR/sensor capture path before production native implementation.

## Scope

Android only; separate ai.stateaction.spike.capture package and isolated spikes/android/capture source. Preserve the existing collector and the recording engineer's checkout. Candidate 1080p30, Main 4.0, no B frames, 12 Mb/s target and one-second IDR; all settings remain unqualified until measured.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Build a standalone APK and record exact source/APK/device/OS/encoder versions.
- [ ] On the physical Android device, capture original camera frame IDs/times, hardware H.264 Annex B access units in generic-profile MCAP, independent raw accel/gyro and matching raster/calibration; record actual tracking/depth/confidence availability and gaps.
- [ ] Verify actual profile/no-B/IDRs, acquisition-to-PTS identity, configuration packets, bounded queues/counts, EOS/close and two consecutive sessions.
- [ ] Run an initial 10–20-minute capture and report actual bytes, cadence, dropped frames, RAM, battery/heat and hand/tool detail. It does not replace two-hour release qualification.
- [ ] Record pass/fail/pending for every criterion with reproducible commands and artifact hashes; emulator or synthetic results never count as physical hardware proof.

## Current execution

Dedicated capture agent is implementing the isolated harness. ADB initially reports no attached device; user has been asked to connect/unlock/authorize it. Continue build and controlled fixture work while waiting.

## Validation and decision

Evidence lives in the ignored artifacts directory and a non-sensitive checked-in receipt. Report whether to keep the candidate, explicitly revise the profile, or stop for an identified blocker. No cloud/GPU spending is needed. Owner discipline: Android/mobile engineer with robotics review. No invented assignee/date/estimate.

Planning key: SA-MVP/SPIKE-ANDROID-CAPTURE

review.title: Spike: Android H.264 MCAP through CPU hands and the real Rerun web viewer
review.description:
## Outcome

Prove the proposed Android source format reaches usable local review before production processing and UI integration.

## Scope

Isolated spikes/android/processing harness using Python 3.12, Rerun SDK/viewer 0.41.0, MediaPipe 1.2.0 and PyAV 19.0.2. Begin with synthetic mixed MCAP and optionally a clearly labelled H.264 transcode of the retained historical Android JPEG capture; then consume the new native sample from <issue id="3bd2ac54-e823-4dc3-8b91-243133928313" href="https://linear.app/hw-personal-projects/issue/SA-60/spike-android-hardware-h264-capture-with-original-sensor-evidence">SA-60</issue>. No full backend/workflow or cloud deployment is required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Read generic MCAP with actual Foxglove Protobuf CompressedVideo descriptors and CDR/JSON evidence; preserve exact original event/frame IDs, clocks and encoder PTS/time bases.
- [ ] Decode once for real CPU hand inference; no-hand frames are masked, not fabricated detections. Report observed detections separately from anatomical/metric accuracy.
- [ ] Remux IDR-safe native MP4 clips with clip_pts=source_pts-first_included_source_pts, retaining original timing; reject malformed config, unsupported B frames and ambiguous mappings.
- [ ] Generate bounded clip-safe H.264 RRD and load it in the actual self-hosted 0.41.0 WASM viewer. Verify playback, seeking, overlay timing, browser/runtime errors and basic memory behavior; an HTML/SVG stand-in is not evidence.
- [ ] Record reproducible fixtures, source/model/config/artifact hashes, passed failure cases and remaining limitations. Synthetic/replay-derived input never qualifies new phone hardware capture.
- [ ] Run the native Android sample when available; otherwise leave that criterion pending and keep the spike open.

## Current execution

Dedicated processing agent is building the harness in parallel. The isolated package/model/three-frame serialization smoke already passed previously; full MCAP/browser and physical-source checks remain new work.

## Dependencies and decision

<issue id="3bd2ac54-e823-4dc3-8b91-243133928313" href="https://linear.app/hw-personal-projects/issue/SA-60/spike-android-hardware-h264-capture-with-original-sensor-evidence">SA-60</issue> supplies the physical source. Synthetic and historical-source replay can proceed while the device is unavailable. Decide compatibility and necessary adapter changes before production reader/viewer work. Owner discipline: robotics/backend engineer with Android/web review. No paid GPU/cloud jobs, invented assignee/date/estimate or changes to original sources.

Planning key: SA-MVP/SPIKE-ANDROID-REVIEW

upload.title: Spike: Android native authentication and background multipart recovery
upload.description:
## Outcome

Prove the Android native session/control and OS transfer path before implementing the production background uploader.

## Scope

Separate ai.stateaction.spike.upload APK plus local Node/TypeScript control/provider-shaped fixture in spikes/android/upload. Android API34+ UIDT visible Upload/Resume; explicitly identify older-API support or pending fallback. Use one source, frozen 64 MiB parts, two PUTs, three temporary chunks and owner/transportEpoch journal. The production Google/Better Auth flow must remain distinct from fixture authentication.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Build an isolated APK and runnable local byte-verifying control fixture; never replace the production collector or modify its pending uploads.
- [ ] Native session client applies secure cookie rotation and renews deliberately short-lived part URLs independently of Dart; only the API signs/reconciles/completes provider state.
- [ ] Exercise interruption/reconciliation, exact part sizes/hashes, bounded retry/space and stale epoch/owner denial. Label fixture/S3-shaped behavior simulated; it is not R2 qualification.
- [ ] On the physical phone, test UIDT permissions/notification/constraints, suspension, screen lock, network change, process stop/reopen and cookie/URL expiry. Persist landed parts and original-owner state.
- [ ] Verify real signed-build native Google ID-token -> Better Auth login and same-owner reauthentication using actual configured audiences; missing credentials/device remains an explicit pending gate, never passed by a test account.
- [ ] Record measured outcomes, commands/build/artifact hashes and a clear OS recovery/UX decision. Leave unexecuted physical/provider/auth cases pending; do not mark the spike Done from local fixture tests alone.

## Current execution

Dedicated upload agent is implementing the isolated Android/native and local-control harness. ADB initially reports no attached phone. No production Google configuration has yet been verified for this separate package.

## Decision and boundaries

Determine whether native URL/session renewal and UIDT recovery work under supported OS conditions, or where the app must show Resume/reopen. No promise of unlimited background execution. No cloud provisioning, paid resources, existing-app replacement, fabricated assignee/date/estimate or production upload mutations.

Planning key: SA-MVP/SPIKE-ANDROID-UPLOAD
